version.changelog:
First release of the Sparki Video Editor skill for OpenClaw.

Features

- CLI with full command set: setup, upload, upload-tg, assets, edit, status, download, history, run
- End-to-end workflow (sparki run): upload, edit, poll, download in a single command
- Two editing modes: Style-Guided (pick from style catalog) and Prompt-Driven (natural language description)
- Style catalog: 20 styles across 7 categories (Vlog, Montage, Commentary, Talking Head, Long-to-Short, AI Caption, Video Resizer)
- Telegram Mini App integration: upload-tg command returns the Mini App upload link for uploading via Telegram
- Structured JSON output: all commands return {"ok": true/false, "data": ..., "error": ...} for reliable AI parsing
- Configuration management: API key stored in ~/.openclaw/config/sparki.json with environment variable override (SPARKI_API_KEY)
- Local project history: tracks recent task IDs for quick history lookups
- SKILL.md dispatch document: complete instructions for OpenClaw bot to guide users through video editing workflows

llm.summary: The skill's code, runtime instructions, and declared permissions are largely consistent with an AI-video-editing CLI that talks to Sparki's API, with only minor mismatches to review before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (Sparki AI video editing) matches the included CLI code: uploading assets, creating projects, polling status, and downloading results. Declared primary credential SPARKI_API_KEY and network domain agent-api.sparki.io align with the API client code.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to run the sparki CLI commands (setup, upload, upload-tg, run/edit/status/download) and to ask users for file paths or use the Telegram upload link. The runtime instructions and the CLI behavior are consistent and limited to uploading/processing video assets and interacting with Sparki. It explicitly forbids local ffmpeg/manual edits, which matches the code's remote-rendering design.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is labeled instruction-first and has no complex installer, but it requires the external 'uv' binary and references 'uv sync' as the install action. Requiring 'uv' (Astral's tool) to sync/install the CLI is unusual but not inherently malicious; it does impose an external install step that fetches code via the uv tool. Review or run setup.sh manually before installing if you want to inspect network activity.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Primary credential SPARKI_API_KEY is appropriate for the service. However, the code also reads SPARKI_UPLOAD_TG_LINK (to override the Telegram upload link) from the environment, but this env var is not listed in the skill metadata/requirements. The metadata lists no required env vars (though primaryEnv is set), which is a mild inconsistency you should be aware of.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true and uses normal autonomous invocation. Its disk writes are limited to the skill's config and workspace under ~/.openclaw (saving API key, history, and downloaded outputs), which is proportionate to its functionality. It does not modify other skills or system-wide settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: it uploads local videos or handles Telegram uploads, creates edit projects on Sparki, and downloads results. Before installing: 1) Confirm you are comfortable giving the Sparki API key (SPARKI_API_KEY) — the CLI stores it under ~/.openclaw/config. 2) Note the skill may read any file path you provide (it requires read access to $CWD); only give paths to files you intend to upload. 3) The install requires the external 'uv' tool (uv sync); inspect setup.sh and consider manually running it to see what it downloads. 4) The code reads SPARKI_UPLOAD_TG_LINK from the environment but that env var wasn’t declared in the metadata — if you rely on a custom upload link, set that env var or verify the stored config. 5) If you need higher assurance, review network traffic (agent-api.sparki.io) and confirm the Telegram upload link and Sparki endpoints are expected. Overall the skill is coherent with its purpose but exercise the usual caution with API keys and external installers.
